pr_title: fix(nuxt): avoid throwing 404 error before middleware finishes
pr_body:
### 🔗 Linked issue
Fixes: https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/issues/29051
Fixes: https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/issues/27903

<!-- Please ensure there is an open issue and mention its number. For example, "resolves #123" -->

### 📚 Description

<!-- Describe your changes in detail. Why is this change required? What problem does it solve? -->

<!----------------------------------------------------------------------
Before creating the pull request, please make sure you do the following:

- Check that there isn't already a PR that solves the problem the same way. If you find a duplicate, please help us reviewing it.
- Read the contribution docs at https://nuxt.com/docs/community/contribution

Thank you for contributing to Nuxt!

It seems that since Nuxt 3.12.0, there are cases where a 404 error occurs before a global middleware redirect.
This is because the 404 is thrown before the middleware is executed.
ref: https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/27016
pr_comments: _Run & review this pull request in [StackBlitz Codeflow](https://stackblitz.com/~/github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/29054)._

I think maybe these lines prevent rendering HTML that won't be returned. Or the following would occur:

- we know there's a 404 but go ahead and render `app.vue` -> this needs to be avoided
- we then render `error.vue`

If that's the case we could guard with `if (import.meta.server)`.

We also need to verify that removing them will still show a 404 page correctly if rendering with `ssr: false`.

(Unfortunately they don't seem to be covered with tests so maybe implementing tests for the correct behaviour here - and in the linked issue - would be a good first step.)

@danielroe 
Thank you! I'm thinking of adding tests, but are there any tests written for `ssr: false` somewhere?
We use `routeRules` to test it within the basic fixture.

~Due to this fix, a 404 was no longer displayed.~ I fixed it so that a 404 is displayed
The reason the test is not failing is that if `[...slug].vue` exists and the result of validate is false, a 404 is displayed.

issue_context.title: 404 error when using navigateTo in a middleware
issue_context.body:
### Environment

------------------------------
- Operating System: Windows_NT
- Node Version:     v21.6.2
- Nuxt Version:     3.12.2
- CLI Version:      3.12.0
- Nitro Version:    2.9.6
- Package Manager:  bun@1.1.15
- Builder:          -
- User Config:      telemetry, devtools, typescript, modules, ssr, i18n, app, image, security, pwa, googleFonts, ui, colorMode, vcalendar, css, vite, nitro, runtimeConfig, eslint, tailwindcss      
- Runtime Modules:  nuxt-security@1.4.3, @vite-pwa/nuxt@0.8.1, @nuxtjs/i18n@8.3.1, @nuxt/ui@2.17.0, @nuxtjs/google-fonts@3.2.0, @pinia/nuxt@0.5.1, @nuxt/image@1.7.0, @samk-dev/nuxt-vcalendar@1.0.3,
 @vueuse/nuxt@10.11.0, nuxt-applicationinsights@0.3.4, @nuxt/eslint@0.3.13
- Build Modules:    -
------------------------------

### Reproduction

https://stackblitz.com/edit/github-mz7brn?file=package.json

Run the app, navigate to `/auth/login`, you're automatically redirected to `/fr/auth/login`
Now change the version in package.json to Nuxt 3.12+ (3.12.2 for example), do the same thing and you get a 404 error.

### Describe the bug

After upgrading to Nuxt 3.12, Nuxt throws a 404 error when trying to redirect from a page that doesn't exist in the router using a middleware.
SSR is disabled on some specific routes, through Nitro config, which seems to be the source of the issue.
```
  nitro: {
    routeRules: {
      '/': {
        ssr: false,
      },
      '/**': {
        ssr: false,
      },
    },
  },
```

EDIT: this can even be simplified. Just having `ssr: false` in the Nuxt config causes the issue.

### Additional context

_No response_

### Logs

> [nuxt] error caught during app initialization Error: Page not found: /auth/login

> 
> [stackblitz.com/edit/github-mz7brn-gkhhkt?file=pages%2Findex.vue,middleware%2Fdefault.global.ts](https://stackblitz.com/edit/github-mz7brn-gkhhkt?file=pages%2Findex.vue,middleware%2Fdefault.global.ts)

I see that you've added a link on the home page to reach `/auth/login`
This is indeed working. To reproduce the bug, you need to go directly on `/auth/login` by typing it in the address bar.

![image](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/assets/334940/0ba14f92-dff3-442d-9d72-14fde6eb0191)

This is somewhat expected - you only have `~/pages/[lang]/auth/login.vue` and so `/auth/login` is not a valid page.

As a workaround, you can update it to `~/pages/[[lang]]/auth/login.vue` - the `[[` indicates an optional parameter.

This was caused by https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/27016, which runs middleware _earlier_ in the lifecycle. Because of the difference between ssr/non-ssr behaviour I'd consider it a bug.

review_comments: If this process is registered before `beforeEach`, it will be executed before the global middleware. Therefore, it needs to be registered after `beforeEach`.
is it sufficient to move it?

Yes, simply moving this was sufficient. If there is no middleware that performs a redirect, a 404 is displayed. 
If there is middleware that performs a redirect, I have confirmed that the issue is resolved with the redirect.

This issue wasn't detected in the tests because [...slug].vue exists, so I'm considering fixing the tests, but I plan to do it in a separate PR.
